The candy bowl in a community bank lobby is the single best underwriting signal nobody models.

Full-size name brand candy means the bank is growing, flush, and probably overpaying for deposits. Fancy imported mints means a consultant came through and the efficiency ratio is about to get worse.

You want the off-brand strawberry hard candies in the crinkly wrapper. The ones that have been in that bowl since the Bush administration. That is a bank that has never once spent a dollar it didn't have to.

0.7x book. Buy it.

candidates.text:
The Nvidia board statement is predictably weaker than Jensen’s statement. Their job was to build credibility and trust, and they undermine that by making it seem like their minds are made up already

Good:
- focused on the national security angle (as opposed to the personal misconduct)
- short

Bad:
- expressing “full confidence” before the investigation is done makes it sound like they’ve already decided the result. Never do this; it wrecks the perceived neutrality of the investigation and makes the findings seem biased 
- if the investigation is truly “independent” then you need to name who’s doing it, because their credibility determines how credible the investigation is
- saying “we have no reason to believe” any secrets were compromised when that is the very thing being questioned
